title: Android Wire native runtime dependency and qualification boundary
summary: The Android renderer is downstream of a separately qualified embedded ooRexx runtime. Resolve semantic package dependencies separately from target-native ELF and APK installability. Do not infer handset qualification from static ELF closure.
invariants: Keep Wire UI semantic state, event identity and application behavior independent of Android JNI and renderer implementation.
Minimal bootstrap is Android/Bionic, the JNI host, embedded ooRexx and its verified native dependencies; do not make RexxOS Grid transports, storage or Queue Fabric mandatory for Wire.
Resolve and lock exact semantic package versions and hashes before hosted Wire composition; separately verify ABI, SONAME/DT_NEEDED, ELF architecture and native target loadability.
Require exact correspondence between Java native method declaration and JNI symbol or explicit RegisterNatives mapping.
Treat APK package installation, Java library load, JNI invocation, interpreter creation, CallProgram and Wire activation as distinct qualification gates.
Use dev22-fixed as the last handset-confirmed JNI proof; dev23 and dev24 are not accepted runtime or packaging baselines.
Do not claim handset qualification from an archive inspection, static readelf audit or build success.
Runtime Reference execution routing, Runtime Registry module generation and Deployment reconciliation are distinct contracts.

evidence.status: handset JNI proof confirmed in prior acceptance; nativeProbe returned 12345
source checkpoint, not an installed application
static ARM64 ELF dependency audit only
dependency closure precedent; not an Android runtime artifact

authority: Documentation and qualification contract only; does not supersede Wire UI server behavioral authority or certify APK deployment.
